more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain fruit wine and made wine.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: 240 mg tartaric acid/kg body weight/day, included in the combined L-tartaric acid and tartrate group (EFSA, 2020).
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA found no concern at reported food-use levels.
The assessment assumes conversion to L-tartaric acid before systemic exposure.
more_info.overview: Metatartaric acid is an esterified material derived from tartaric acid; its chemical form changes as it hydrolyses in water. Its emulsifying role is to help form or maintain mixtures of oil and water in the finished food. The specified material is supplied as white powder or crystalline material. The specification identifies water solubility as one of its properties.
